assertion.value:
As a part of the dataset creation process, we carefully review the pipeline at every stage, ensuring there is no personally identifiable information or offensive content, either during data collection or through the use of LLMs. For all purposes, we create dummy accounts that mimic real-like user content. To get the gold labels scripts we seek help from well-qualified student workers, approved through the institution, and get the bounding box data annotated through MTurk workers, both of whom are paid
                      
                      per hour, which is greater than the minimum wage rate (We detail this process in the supplementary material). Human studies are also done with the help of student workers approved by the institution at the above-mentioned payscale. We also ensure that all groups have equitable representation and that no personal opinions are reflected in the dataset, avoiding bias during the collection as well as the annotation process.

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents an IoT-based monitoring system deployed for tomato cultivation in Mandya, Karnataka, India's Eastern Dry Zone. The system collects soil NPK, temperature, humidity, pH, and electrical conductivity data at 2-hour intervals over a 110- day growth cycle, yielding 1,320 synchronized time points. Using this dataset, we evaluate machine learning models for detecting nutrient deficiency diseases including chlorosis, purpling, and leaf scorch. XGBoost achieves 84.3% accuracy and a macro-average F1-score of 0.84, while Random Forest predicts NPK concentrations with RMSEs of 28.4 ppm (N), 22.1 ppm (P), and 35.2 ppm (K). Correlation analysis identifies nitrogen levels (r = -0.45, p < 0.01) as the strongest predictor of disease manifestation. As a pilot study with single-season, single-location data, the results establish a baseline for future multiyear validation.</jats:p>
title: A Field-Deployed Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for IoT-Enabled Tomato Crop Monitoring

items.abstract: This paper introduces RedTeamAI, a novel benchmark designed to rigorously evaluate the cybersecurity capabilities of autonomous agents powered by large language models.RedTeamAI provides a structured environment with diversecybersecurity challenges, ranging from vulnerability discoveryto exploit development, enabling detailed assessment of agentperformance. The benchmark facilitates the analysis of agentstrengths and weaknesses in offensive security scenarios, contributing to a deeper understanding of the potential risks andapplications of AI in cybersecurity. Experimental results demonstrate the framework’s utility in characterizing the adversarialproficiency of current language model agents.
title: RedTeamAI: A Benchmark for Assessing Autonomous Cybersecurity Agents
